title: pwmd operator RPC: runtime log verbosity and focus control
mvp_checklist: docs/api-v1.md operator endpoints outside stable public contract
brief: Add an authorized operator/debug RPC surface for changing pwmd log verbosity and focus at runtime, so operators can temporarily increase detail around a target subsystem without generating megabytes of always-on debug logs. Start with a short specification, then implement through the normal pwm-coding -> pwm-testing -> pwm-review conveyor.
requirements: Operator/debug endpoint, not public stable API.
Must be authorization-gated or loopback/dev-mode gated; no unauthenticated remote verbosity control.
Must support scoped focus filters such as transport:peers, sync:live, seal:loop, snapshot, api.
Must support TTL/auto-expire to restore baseline logging.
Must avoid changing consensus or wire semantics.

slices.title: Map current pwmd API and logging architecture
acceptance: pwm-info identifies router entry points, logging filter setup, file/peer log sinks, and safe place for runtime control state.
The map calls out what can be done without restarting tracing subscriber and what requires reloadable filter support.

slices.title: Operator RPC specification
acceptance: Spec defines endpoints, auth/gating, request/response payloads, TTL, focus names, and audit events.
Spec explicitly keeps the endpoints outside public stable /v1 contract.
Spec defines a minimal implementation profile for the first coding slice.

slices.title: Runtime log control implementation
acceptance: Operator can set temporary runtime log level/focus and inspect/reset current override.
Unauthorized/non-loopback access is rejected according to the spec.

slices.title: Tests and independent review
acceptance: pwm-testing passes focused tests and documents any manual smoke.

notes: Created after MVP V3 closeout. Owner requested a specification and implementation slice for authorized pwmd RPC endpoints that dynamically control logging verbosity/focus during runtime. pwm-info confirmed current logging is static EnvFilter with no reload support, API state is App via axum router, current auth pattern is dev_profile only, and recommended profile is tracing_subscriber reload layer plus loopback-or-Bearer operator endpoints. Orchestrator drafted docs/rfc/17-runtime-log-control-rpc.md and linked it from docs/api-v1.md and docs/pwmd.md. pwm-coding implemented reloadable runtime filter control, operator GET/POST/DELETE endpoints with loopback-or-token auth gate (`PWM_ADMIN_TOKEN`), strict payload validation, TTL auto-restore, `pwmd::operator` audit events, and focused HTTP tests for set/get/delete, invalid focus/ttl, remote rejection, token auth, and TTL expiry restore. pwm-testing gate (Windows, isolated CARGO_TARGET_DIR=F:\pwm-test\PWM-cryptocurrency): `cargo fmt --check`, `check_entity_name_segments.py` on touched pwmd Rust files (clean), `cargo check -p pwmd --lib`, `cargo test -p pwmd op_log_` — initial 6/6 PASS (pre-extra tests). Docs cross-check: operator class outside §2 freeze OK; PWM_ADMIN_TOKEN + loopback wording matches lifecycle.rs + handlers_operator_log.rs; TTL 1..=3600 + focus names match RFC table; docs use placeholder Bearer form (no leaked secrets). Nit follow-up by pwm-coding: replaced fixed sleep in `op_log_ttl_restore` with bounded polling loop, added explicit `remote + token configured + wrong Bearer` test (expects 403 and verifies override unchanged), and added lightweight real TCP smoke test for operator log endpoint over loopback socket. pwm-testing re-verify post-nit-fix: same gate commands; `op_log_` 8/8 PASS. Residual: no dedicated long-lived external process smoke; TCP smoke covers live listener + raw HTTP on loopback. pwm-review: independent report in artifacts.review_md; APPROVE_WITH_NITS (see delegations[pwm-review].notes). Orchestrator closeout: accepted low-priority owner-decision nits as follow-up (constant-time bearer compare, audit reason, reverse-proxy ops note); ticket status set to done.
